content: {"summary":"Fraud‑scorer writes were refused because Redis entered MISCONF when its background snapshot failed. The snapshot fork could not allocate memory due to a strict overcommit setting (vm.overcommit_memory=2, 80% ratio), causing Redis to stop accepting writes even though only 14 GB of 32 GB were used.","likely_cause":"Strict memory overcommit setting (vm.overcommit_memory=2) caused snapshot fork failures, triggering Redis MISCONF and write refusals.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Redis memory usage was well within limits","evidence_ids":["INC-0078#0"],"quote":"Redis held about 14 GB on a 32 GB VM, comfortably inside its own limits."},{"text":"Writes were refused because snapshot attempts failed, causing Redis to stop accepting writes","evidence_ids":["INC-0078#1"],"quote":"snapshot attempts were failing, and Redis stops accepting writes"},{"text":"Snapshot fork failed due to strict memory accounting limiting commitments to 25.6 GB","evidence_ids":["INC-0078#1"],"quote":"strict memory accounting (`vm.overcommit_memory = 2`, ratio 80) caps total commitments at 25.6 GB"},{"text":"Resetting the overcommit setting allowed snapshots to finish and writes to resume","evidence_ids":["INC-0078#2"],"quote":"and writes were accepted again"}],"next_checks":["Verify that other redis‑features hosts do not have vm.overcommit_memory set to 2","Add monitoring for Redis background save failures and MISCONF errors","Review baseline sysctl configuration to prevent strict overcommit on Redis nodes"]}
